title: Trend Following in 2025- New Challenges, New Strategies! - Systematic Investor 326

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Trend Following in 2025- New Challenges, New Strategies! - Systematic Investor 326.docx

speakers: Alan Dunne (host this week, sitting in for Niels; caption 'Alan Dunn')
summary: Systematic Investor 326 (Dec 2024): Alan Dunne and Katie Kaminski review 2024 trend performance via CTA style factors (slow beat fast, large beat small markets), the BlackRock managed futures ETF filing, Quantica's paper on volatility sizing, and Aspect's portable alpha paper. Conclusions: speed explains dispersion in 2024, dynamic volatility sizing trades return for Sharpe and reduces concentration, and portable alpha carries correlation risk; inflation volatility is the key 2025 risk.

coverage.note: Intro; Dec 2024 CTA performance and sector moves (softs, European equities)
November currency trend, Trump trade, 2024 themes, CTA style factors defined
2024 style factor results: slow minus big, fixed income speed asymmetry, dispersion
Commodity correlation factor, speed regression of managers, cross-asset correlation
Size factor in equities; BlackRock managed futures ETF filing and product lifecycle
Hedge Nordic roundtable, replication, optimism about 2025, trend likes stress
Dollar trade risks, sentiment warning, Quantica volatility sizing paper start
Long vol link, vol rising into profitable trades and reversals, static vs dynamic spectrum
Sharpe vs return result, two philosophies on concentration, hit rate
Rare profitable trends, behavioral give-back, rates vol expansion, sample limits
Long volatility exposure and sizing, concentration in risk factors, macro themes
Macro theme exposure of trend, 2024 lack of macro change, start of portable alpha discussion
Portable alpha correlation risk, futures capital efficiency, packaging
Complexity, opportunity cost, classification of hybrid products
Bucket comparison, 130/30, tweaking trend for equity blend, combined drawdown risk
2025 outlook: inflation volatility, bonds, US divergence, tariffs

completeness_estimate: 0.87 - the first reader captured nearly all the style-factor results, Quantica volatility-sizing debate, ETF and portable-alpha points and 2025 risks; misses are secondary remarks (universe-size tilt, endogeneity caveat, discretionary concentration, trend-plus-constant-equity idea); one wrong speaker and one wrong month.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: we've seen breakouts again in in coffee and in Cocoa equities have been trending hard particularly European equities we've seen renewed momentum there
claims.claim: In December 2024 trend followers gained from renewed breakouts in coffee and cocoa and from European equity momentum, while fixed income stayed choppy and the euro was under pressure.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: on the year to dat both up uh just just under 3%
claims.claim: SG CTA and SG Trend indices were up about 1.7 percent in December 2024 and just under 3 percent for the year.
claims.indicator: SG CTA Index, SG Trend Index

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: last month you know everyone was talking about that Trump trade right so the long equities long dollar and maybe a little bit of short and fixed income
claims.claim: The post-election 'Trump trade' in October and November 2024 was long equities, long dollar and short fixed income, which trend followers followed.
claims.direction: long equities, long USD, short bonds

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: the biggest mover and thing to watch out of all that trade in November really has been currencies
claims.claim: Currencies were the most consistent trend in November 2024, unusual for trend following.

correction.issue: Wrong month. Katie answers Alan's question about this month (December 2024): the currency trade is the biggest mover this month, after last month's (November) Trump trade of long equities, long dollar and short fixed income.
correction.fix: Currencies were the biggest and most consistent trend in December 2024, following November's Trump-trade positioning; currencies do not usually drive trend returns, but when they work it is exciting.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: q1 was you know guns blazing it was phenomenal quarter like it was you know you had equities up you had commodities doing well
claims.claim: 2024 was a false start and re-emergence for trend: a strong Q1 (equities, commodities), back-and-forth Q2 and Q3 on monetary policy, relief after the election in Q4, summarised as 'slow and steady wins the race'.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: they kind of take a plane transist and then they perturbate some of the designed decisions within the system to isolate a factor of decision
claims.claim: CTA style factors perturb one design decision of a plain trend system versus a benchmark to isolate speed, size, co-movement and correlation tilts, explaining return dispersion across managers.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: so are you faster or slower than your peer set
claims.claim: The speed factor measures whether a trend system is faster or slower than the peer set.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: how much do you allocate to smaller versus larger markets
claims.claim: The size factor measures allocation to smaller versus larger markets, analogous to the equity size factor.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: this is meant as a proxy for crowded trades
claims.claim: The co-movement factor, inspired by Nick Baltas, proxies for crowded trades.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: how much do you lean into less correlated markets versus more correlated markets so the dollar versus like the Mexican peso for example
claims.claim: The correlation factor measures leaning into less correlated versus more correlated markets.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: slow systems had very highly positive returns and faster Sy system signals had much much worse negative returns and this was true across all asset classes
claims.claim: In 2024 slow-minus-fast was massively positive across all asset classes: slow systems earned strongly and fast signals lost, because following the long-term trend avoided monetary policy noise.
claims.conditions: year dominated by monetary policy flip-flops

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: large markets perform better than small markets and this was particularly the case for Equity indices
claims.claim: Large markets beat small markets in 2024, especially equity indices (S&P 500, Nasdaq), while co-movement and correlation factors mattered little.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: some managers got long fixed income I think maybe in December and did did well then but then did badly in January when the markets reversed
claims.claim: Dispersion in 2024 came from fixed income positioning: fast flips between rate cut hopes, sticky inflation, recession fears and the Trump trade punished fast signals.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: anything in the shorter term around six months or less pet really struggled in fixed income
claims.claim: Trend signals with lookbacks of about six months or less struggled in fixed income in 2024 while 10-month plus signals did better.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: I don't think it was exceptionally larger than sort of certain years in general
claims.claim: Dispersion across trend managers in 2024 was not exceptionally large versus other years, mostly in Q1, Q2 and Q4.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: the correlation factor for Commodities was positive and that kind of you know might suggest that like less correlated markets uh did a little better especially for Commodities
claims.claim: Within commodities in 2024 the correlation factor was positive: less correlated markets such as cocoa and coffee did better than energies and metals.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: when we looked at the regression outputs for Speed versus performance it has a remarkably good fit to sort of what you see
claims.claim: Regressing managers' 2024 returns on the speed factor explains the range from -5 to +10 percent; speed tilt separates crisis-alpha seekers from slow replication ETFs.
claims.indicator: speed factor coefficient vs manager return

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: reactivity is important in Trend but um each year is different
claims.claim: Reactivity pays in recessions or events while slow wins in other years, so speed must be balanced over time.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: fixed income has been sort of positively correlated with Equity sometimes and then negatively correlated other times
claims.claim: Inflation made cross-asset correlations vary in the last 2 to 3 years; fixed income flipped between positive and negative correlation with equities, complicating bond trend.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you were a slow Trend follower heavily f Fus on the S&P you probably did quite well this year
claims.claim: A slow trend follower focused on the S&P did well in 2024 while European equities and the Hang Seng were choppy.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: changes in US regulation have really made active ETFs a much more viable product structure
claims.claim: Regulatory changes in the US made active ETFs viable, supporting the managed futures ETF wave including BlackRock's filing.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: there's product proliferation then there's Innovation and consolidation and then maturation
claims.claim: New product spaces go through proliferation, innovation and consolidation, and maturation phases; managed futures ETFs are in proliferation.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: replication is an exciting way to to to get exposure but we combine you know we think about combining it with bottom up approaches like direct implementation and risk management
claims.claim: Replication is useful for managed futures exposure but is better combined with bottom-up implementation and risk management.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: trend is a strategy that likes macr change and stress
claims.claim: Trend likes macro change and stress; when typical equity investors are not stressed, trend consolidates.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: Trend goes through periods of consolidation and then it goes through periods that you know of really finding incredible Trends
claims.claim: Trend returns come in cycles of consolidation and strong trending, and timing the change is not possible.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: dollar trade the US versus you know other has some some legs but you know of course there's also risk there's you know policy mistakes there's you know geopolitical conflict that could get in the middle and trade conflict
claims.claim: The US-vs-world dollar trade had legs in Dec 2024 but faced risks of policy mistakes, geopolitical conflict and trade conflict, creating turbulence trend likes.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: notable bears capitulating under bearish views which is always a kind of a a warning sign that maybe things are getting really over exuberant
claims.claim: Equity sentiment at an all-time high and bears capitulating is a warning sign of over-exuberance, though it cannot be timed.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: if you're going to trade a trend do you sort of buy a certain number of contracts and like hold it out to a certain level or do you sort of buy it and then size it as volatility increases
claims.claim: Quantica's paper tests static contract sizing versus dynamic volatility sizing over 30 years.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: it was only 1.05 for you know ratio of increase in volatility for sort of losing trades but they found that the winning trades had a volatility ratio of 1.2
claims.claim: Volatility from entry to exit rose by only 1.05 times in losing trades but 1.2 times in winning trades, and the biggest winners had the highest increase.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: there's like a 20% correlation and that's just the ballpark between manage Futures Trend and ball
claims.claim: Managed futures trend is about 20 percent correlated with long volatility.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: a classic Trend with static position probably has a 40% or higher uh correlation with long Vall
claims.claim: Static-sized trend probably has 40 percent or higher correlation with long volatility, while dynamic sizing reduces over-concentration in a few trades.
claims.indicator: trend long vol exposure by sizing method

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: how volatility tends to rise into profitable trades and and that's something we intuitively know
claims.claim: Volatility tends to rise during profitable trends, giving trend a residual long-vol profile.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: it went from say I think 20% annualized fall to 120% it hit to 120% when it started to turn down from the peak
claims.claim: Realised cocoa volatility went from about 20 to 120 percent at the turn from the peak, supporting volatility sizing because volatility spikes at reversals.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: you can actually think about this as a spectrum right so if you thought about the static is if you treat the volatility is irrelevant and the dynamic is like you're moving with it a lot
claims.claim: Static versus dynamic sizing is a spectrum determined by how volatility is measured and how reactive the system is.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you did get a higher return albeit with higher V and a lower sharp
claims.claim: Quantica's data: volatility scaling gives higher Sharpe, while static sizing gives higher return at higher volatility and lower Sharpe, so both camps are right.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you do want to have that concentration to capture the possible outlier
claims.claim: Classic trend followers want concentration in volatile winners to capture outliers, while statistical portfolio managers see no reason to concentrate there.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: there's just not that many things that Trend or that often but when they do if you have the strategy you capture most of your you know it's that positive skewness
claims.claim: Few markets trend and not often, but when they do the strategy captures large positive-skew payoffs (cocoa 2024), unlike hit rates in equity or value.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: these are trends that are extremely profitable but rare and not 50% of the time
claims.claim: Choose between capturing the most return from rare trends with reversal vulnerability or a smoother, more risk-managed ride.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you make 10 15% in q1 but then give it back quickly it tends to annoy people
claims.claim: Investors dislike large early-year gains being given back, creating behavioural pressure for smoother sizing.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: actually the move in in interest rates is even more extreme
claims.claim: Volatility expansion in SOFR and 2-year note contracts was an even greater multiple than in cocoa, showing such trades require patience.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you're searching for outliers presumbly are just you are searching for quite infrequent so in another 30-year period you could have more outliers and and the results could be could be uh could be different
claims.claim: The Quantica 30-year sample (1994 to 2024) relies on infrequent outliers, so results could differ in another period; blends with equities and skewness were not analysed.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: we do have residual long Vol exposure because when things Trend the volatility tends to have expanded
claims.claim: Managed futures are not explicitly long volatility but carry residual long-vol exposure because trending markets see volatility expand.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: maybe they can get more correlation to the long V you know if they have the static
claims.claim: For risk-mitigation seekers static sizing offers more long-vol correlation, aggressive sizing gives better risk-adjusted return; a mix of both may suit investors.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you're vola sizing you can be concentrated on a risk factor sometimes you know as you know inflation was a big driver effectively we you know most CTS kind of were effectively short bonds you know back in 22
claims.claim: Volatility-sized trend can still be concentrated on one macro factor; in 2022 most CTAs were effectively short bonds on inflation.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: when you look at it across a portfolio it's really exposed to prevailing Market macro themes
claims.claim: Trend is exposed across the portfolio to prevailing macro themes and their correlation structure and stability.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: a lot of the overall volatility profile correlation profile has been really focused on monetary policy
claims.claim: In the last 2 to 3 years volatility and correlation profiles have focused on monetary policy and inflation, driving the stock-bond correlation.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: those individual building blocks build up to something that really is a macro themed exposure based purely on price movements
claims.claim: Trend positions aggregate into a macro-themed exposure built purely from price moves.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: it's sort of a systematic approach to get that macro exposure without having to make all the macro calls
claims.claim: An investor reason to use trend: macro exposure without making macro calls or timing central banks.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: there hasn't been a lot of macro change so it's not surprising that you know that hasn't been an easy macro environment in general for Trend especially in shorter time Horizons
claims.claim: 2024 lacked macro change (cut or no cut oscillation), making it a hard year for trend especially at shorter horizons.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: some of the best periods of performance for Trend following tends to be in those periods like U Global financial crisis or we saw again 22 when when markets do tend to get quite correlated
claims.claim: Trend's best periods (GFC, 2022) come when markets are highly correlated and one macro factor dominates.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: the concept of alpha is relative to the risk that you've removed assuming that you caught all of them
claims.claim: In portable alpha, alpha is only relative to the risks removed; investors assume the alpha is segregated from risk when it is not.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: there can be period periods of time where manage fures is doesn't look like Alpha at all where it's actually long equities and that would actually increase your exposure if you had a recession or a draw down
claims.claim: Managed futures can be long equities, so a portable alpha stack has correlation risk and adds to losses in a recession or drawdown.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: implicit in that leverage um you know you don't have the borrowing cost associated with it
claims.claim: Futures give capital-efficient leverage without borrowing cost.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: I'm a big fan of combining equities with Trend and other you know managed future strategies because they naturally work well together
claims.claim: Equities plus trend gives a smoother global portfolio while retaining equity exposure.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: much more of a packaging question I think for people
claims.claim: Combining equities and trend is mostly a packaging question; products will grow but complexity requires investor education.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: the more complex a product becomes um the the harder it is for investors to understand your know performance over time and expectations
claims.claim: Complexity of hybrid products makes it harder for investors to understand performance and expectations.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: part of the reason for the Resurgence of Port of alasa is it's hard to sell an alternative product in an environment where the S&P is doing you know 25% per anom
claims.claim: Portable alpha resurged because alternatives are hard to sell when the S&P returns 25 percent a year and investors perceive an opportunity cost.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: instead of sourcing from pulling out of those two classic buckets maybe you can just kind of add something that has alternative features that's similar to that bucket
claims.claim: Portable alpha lets investors add alternative features to the equity or bond bucket without switching out of 60/40.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: is it in equity bucket or is it not or is it closet equity in your Alternatives bucket
claims.claim: Hybrid return streams create a classification problem between equity and alternatives buckets.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: they created a bucket which you know had a specific mandate and then they could articulate to their portfolio teams and their boards like you know this is the goal of this strategy
claims.claim: Pensions solved classification by creating a risk-mitigation bucket with a specific mandate for trend and long vol.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: once it's in the bucket guess what it gets compared to the things in the bucket
claims.claim: Hybrid products get benchmarked against bucket peers, which complicates attribution and explanation.

correction.issue: Wrong speaker. Katie, not Alan, says that once a hybrid product sits in a bucket it is compared with the other holdings in that bucket (Alan then asks 'is it Equity Plus').
correction.fix: Katie Kaminski says a hybrid equity-plus-trend product is classified into an existing bucket and then benchmarked against that bucket's other holdings, which complicates explanation and attribution.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: dispersion across equities both globally and in the micro level has created a lot more opportunities
claims.claim: 130/30 equity long-short is a natural portable-alpha candidate because cross-sectional dispersion and momentum created opportunities in 2024.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: other managers have looked at things like beta capping Equity exposure
claims.claim: To blend trend with equities, managers dynamically size trend, cap equity beta in the trend book or accept independence.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you will get some months where both equities and Trend following have a tough month and then you're going to have a particularly tough month
claims.claim: Portable alpha has months when equities and trend both lose, producing very tough months.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: the biggest risk and that people are underestimating and I've generally said the volatility of inflation
claims.claim: The risk most underestimated for 2025 is the volatility of inflation, not just its level, given unknown US deficits and policies.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: have no natural Predators except for inflation
claims.claim: Bonds have no natural predator except inflation, so bonds will be hard for both investors and trend, which used to be favoured by managed futures.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: the US is the slower one to cut rates we never you know that's not a usual they're usually leading and now they're they're lying right
claims.claim: The US lagging other regions in cutting rates, a divergence not seen in most careers, makes the pro-US theme worth watching.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: if you did get animal Spurs being Unleashed in the US and the F had to turn and and start a Titan again and the ECB at a point of easing I mean that would be really unprecedented
claims.claim: Tariffs plus animal spirits could force the Fed to tighten while the ECB eases, an unprecedented divergence in recent decades.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: still kind of showing a little bit of stickiness I mean not not not not running away to the upside but certainly not certainly being slow to converge on the magic 2% level
claims.claim: US inflation prints in December 2024 are sticky and slow to converge to 2 percent.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: for a smaller Market set if you have you know 20 or something you definitely have a tilt yes to the bigger markets
claims.claim: A trend program that trades a small universe (around 20 markets) is structurally tilted to large markets such as the S&P 500, so its result in a year like 2024 depends on how many markets it trades; it is effectively a different strategy from a broad one.
claims.indicator: number of markets traded; market-size tilt
claims.testable: yes - compare trend returns by universe size

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: Black Rock getting into the space is just a sign that you know this is a space that could have
claims.claim: BlackRock's managed futures ETF filing signals that managed futures could become a viable allocation inside the disaggregated US pension system, where few people have had access to it.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: everyone else is looking for a bull and we're looking for a bear
claims.claim: Trend followers are constantly alert to a regime break, so their worries are a useful contrarian check on consensus risk: sentiment extremes and capitulating bears are warnings, though the turn cannot be timed.

claims.speaker: Katie Kaminski
claims.quote: endogenous right like you and I know this like obviously if a trend was profitable the volatility is going to be higher
claims.claim: The finding that volatility rose more in winning trades is partly endogenous, because profitable trends mechanically have higher volatility; only the size of the gap between winners and losers (1.2 versus 1.05) is informative.
claims.testable: yes - control for realised move size when comparing trade volatility ratios

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: you don't want to have a balanced with 10 positions if you have a high conviction on the dollar that's where you want to have your risk
claims.claim: A discretionary macro manager concentrates risk in a high-conviction idea by levering up, whereas quant trend programs spread risk statistically, so concentration is a philosophical split between discretionary and systematic styles.

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: my impression is that they were more you were combining equities with another Equity strategy which wasn't very sensible
claims.claim: Pre-crisis portable alpha mostly paired equity beta with another equity-type alpha strategy, which shared the same risk and failed in 2008; today's version pairs equity beta with managed futures that are diversifying.
claims.conditions: alpha source correlated with the beta source

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: why don't trend followers just stick in a you know a constant long uh you know 100% S&P future and then modulate around that
claims.claim: Combining equities with trend improves Sharpe, which suggests a trend program could hold a constant 100 percent long S&P future and modulate around it; this is effectively the same as portable alpha, leaving packaging as the practical difference.
claims.indicator: trend program with embedded equity beta
claims.testable: yes - backtest trend with a fixed 100% equity base versus separate sleeves

claims.speaker: Alan Dunne
claims.quote: polls and expecting a lot of concern about elections and you know we've got through 2024 it's all it's all gone pretty smoothly you would say
claims.claim: Widely anticipated 2024 election risk largely did not disrupt markets, so consensus event-risk worries were over-priced as sources of turbulence.
